We welcome UN Women's growing work on technology innovation, AI, and combating tech-facilitated violence. These efforts should be at the heart of the next Strategic Plan and linked to the implementation of the wider UN commitments and work on technology and innovation. Such as the Global Digital Compact and the World Summit on the Information Society. Sustainable peace is not possible without women's full and meaningful participation at all levels in peace processes. We welcome UN Women's continued focus on peace— women, peace and security agenda. Finally, Finland reaffirms its strong political and financial support to UN Women. We continue to prioritize core funding, and we call on others to do so. Madam President, let's meet this moment with determination. Let's build forward, with gender equality at the centre. Thank you.
I thank the distinguished representative from Finland for his comments. And I now give the floor to the distinguished representative from Switzerland.

Madam President, Madam Executive Director, we thank the Executive Director, Madam Sima Bahus, for her opening statement. This mandate is essential for promoting universal norms in gender equality. It's essential that this role is supported and strengthened. We applaud the firm position adopted in this regard by the new strategic plan. In a difficult context, Switzerland insists on the urgency of the UN system being more agile, and we applaud the emphasis placed by the new strategic plan on digital transformation, adaptability, and proactive risk management. Switzerland is convinced that courageous reforms are possible and that the acceleration of the implementation of existing reform mandates is essential in order to strengthen the impact of the multilateral system. When it comes to the reform of the UN system, Switzerland fully supports an improvement of the operational capacity taking account of the comparative advantages of each agency respectively. This involves enhanced interagency collaboration, better use of shared services, and better coherence in interventions. UN Women must continue to play a leading role in this transformation and fully harness its coordination mandate. Quality financing remains a key tool, and we call for predictable, flexible, and plurianual funding. It's also necessary to plan and act effectively, in particular in these complex contexts and situations of crises. We also welcome the commitment of UN Women for solid, robust accountability mechanisms including audit, ethics, evaluation, and prevention of sexual exploitation, of abuse and harassment. We also applaud the pivot of the UN Women plan to transfer more personnel to Geneva in order to better harness the advantages of the ecosystem. We wish to recall the importance of International Geneva as an essential global hub for multilateralism, humanitarian law, and human rights. Its unique ecosystem is conducive to global dialogue, political innovation, and operational coordination. Switzerland reaffirms here its resolute support to the mandate of UN Women to achieve gender equality, the full achievement of fundamental rights for women and girls, and the empowerment of women. In these difficult times, the work of UN Women is more important than ever. Thank you.

The distinguished representative from Switzerland for his comments. I have the following 3 countries on my list now: Canada, Zimbabwe, and Colombia. The distinguished representative from Canada, you have the floor.

President, um, Madam President, Madam Executive Director, dear colleagues, That SDG 5 is lagging far behind at the global level. Madam President, in a time of growing needs and limited resources, we commend UN Women's leadership on gender-transformative financing and its role in the Financing for Development process. Flexible, predictable funding is essential, not only to increase investment, but to ensure that resources reach those best positioned to drive lasting change. Equally important is the need for inclusion. UN Women's work to dismantle systemic barriers faced by marginalized and structurally excluded groups is essential. We must ensure that gender equality remains at the heart of this transformation. Looking ahead to the 2026 to 2029 Strategic Plan, Canada recognizes the importance of a focused flexible, and results-oriented approach in alignment with the Quadriennial Comprehensive Policy Review. We value high-impact, scalable interventions and streamlined operations that seek to deliver measurable improvements in the lives of all women and girls. Excellencies, colleagues, Canada remains a proud and committed partner, partner to UN Women. Our collective leadership is vital in our ongoing efforts to achieve gender equality, and it is more critical than ever that we work together, continuing to advocate for a world where all women and girls have the freedom, safety, and opportunity to shape their own future with pride and dignity. Merci beaucoup.
I thank the distinguished representative from Canada for his comments. I now give the floor to the distinguished representative from Zimbabwe.

Thank you, Madam President. We extend our sincere appreciation to the Executive Director for a comprehensive report and for underscoring that gender equality remains an unfulfilled solution to many of the world's pressing challenges, including peacebuilding, climate action, economic transformation, and digital inclusion. This reaffirmation is both timely and profoundly important. We note with satisfaction the strides made under the Strategic Plan 2022-2025, particularly in strengthening global normative frameworks, advancing women's leadership, and improving access to gender-responsive services in conflict-affected and humanitarian settings. We are especially grateful for UN Women's support in the development of Zimbabwe's first National Action Plan on Women, Peace and Security in 2024. The visit to Zimbabwe by the Executive Board in May further testifies to the growing and productive partnership between our government and UN Women and provided us with the opportunity to demonstrate the results of this life-changing cooperation. Notwithstanding the progress achieved, we note, however, that structural challenges persist, including entrenched discriminatory norms, underrepresentation of women in decision-making, and high rates of gender-based violence. As highlighted by the Executive Director, investing in care systems is not just a social necessity, but it is a powerful tool for ending poverty. In the context of Zimbabwe's constrained fiscal space and vulnerability to climate shocks, we emphasize the importance of embedding gender equality efforts within resilient, nationally owned systems, which could provide some cover to programs and projects in the face of funding shocks. With regards to the proposed strategic plan for 2026 to 2029, we commend its evidence-based its direction and welcome the emphasis on economic empowerment, leadership, and violence eradication. These priorities reflect the lived realities of women in our region and are consistent with our national agenda. However, the shrinking pool of gender financing requires a fundamental shift toward program sustainability. Future interventions must include program sustainability must include built-in exit strategies, national capacity building, and mechanisms for local resource mobilization to ensure continuity in the face of funding gaps and to avoid disruptions when external funding contracts or ceases. In line with the Executive Director's call to action, we echo the urgency of closing the global $420 billion gender financing gap and call for reforms in global financing frameworks. UN Women's next strategic cycle must also foster stronger partnerships with the African Union and regional economic communities. I wish to conclude by reaffirming Zimbabwe's unwavering commitment to advancing gender equality and the empowerment of women and girls. This commitment is clearly demonstrated through the substantial progress we have made in policy reforms and the implementation of targeted transformative programs aimed at dismantling systemic barriers to equality. Our national efforts continue to focus on unlocking the full potential of women and girls, ensuring their meaningful participation in every sphere of socioeconomic development. We stand ready to continue partnering with UN Women in the realization of a more just and equitable future for all. I thank you.

I thank the distinguished representative from Zimbabwe for her comments. I have the following 3 countries on my list: Latvia, United Kingdom, and Colombia. The distinguished representative from Latvia, you have the floor.

Thank you. Madam President, Executive Director, Excellencies, I wish to express my sincere appreciation to UN Women and to Executive Director Sima Bajos, for your steadfast leadership in advancing gender equality and the empowerment of women and girls. You can count on Latvia's unwavering support for the entity's Triple Mandate. Let me begin by acknowledging the reality we cannot overlook: the growing constraints on the UN budget. Maintaining every programme at its current scale may no longer be feasible. Therefore, we must adopt calibrated, evidence-based responses that prioritize measurable impact. These deliberations should recognize that human rights, including gender equality, have historically received one of the thinnest shares of resources. Encouragingly, UN Women's 13th consecutive audit, with assets outpassing liabilities 9 to 1 attests to exemplary financial stewardship. In this context, Latvia will continue to place gender equality at the center of its national policy and at the heart of our upcoming term on the UN Security Council. In May, Latvia hosted Women, Peace and Security capacity-building workshop under the Asia-Europe Foundation , translating the principles of Resolution 1325 into practical mediation tools for practitioners across both continents. Additionally, the Latvian NGO Riga TechGirls, together with local partners in Egypt, successfully implemented a project that equipped over 100 girls with advanced coding and cyber hygiene skills. Madam President, during our Security Council term, Latvia will prioritize women's rights and leadership by promoting their meaningful participation in peace processes, embedding gender perspectives in climate security responses, and addressing digital threats such as gender disinformation. We take this approach not only because it is right, but because it works. Evidence shows that gender-equal societies are more resilient, less prone to conflict, and better equipped to sustain long-term peace. In conclusion, Latvia reaffirms its steadfast commitment to gender equality and to UN Women's mission. We will continue to provide stable financial support and remain a constructive partner in strengthening the entity's impact. As we navigate a period of difficult decisions, let us not lose sight of what truly drives long-term change. With political will, shared responsibility, and smart investment, we can turn today's commitments into lasting progress for every woman and girl. I thank you.
I thank the distinguished representative from Latvia for his comments, and I now give the floor to the distinguished representative from the United Kingdom.

Thank you, Madam President, and thank you, Executive Director Sima Bahus, for your remarks. As a steadfast advocate for gender equality, the UK appreciates UN Women's continued commitment to advancing gender equality and women and girls' rights globally. In times of increasing political headwinds, your work is critical. Across regions, political and public space for gender equality is shrinking. With widening inequality, protracted crises, and gender equality rollback stalling SDG progress, UN Women's mandate is more important than ever. The UNAT process offers an opportunity to shape a modernized, focused, and impactful UN system. It is critical that gender equality remains central to this. Reform is inevitable and essential, but renegotiation of rights is not. UN Women's active involvement in this process is vital. We would like to ask how UN Women is pushing for accelerated progress on gender equality within broader UN reforms and the 2024 QCPR roadmap? What is your vision for embedding gender equality across interagency reforms, and how can we advance collective impact on this important issue? Looking ahead to the next strategic plan and the progress that needs to be made to deliver the SDGs, the UK supports deeper partnerships and funding models that support grassroots women-led rights organizations. We commend your leadership on women, peace, and security and encourage stronger engagement with human rights mechanisms. Financing remains critical, and like other agencies, UN Women is also under pressure. In that context, we ask that while you continue to look at finding efficiencies, that you do not reduce ambition and or your normative leadership. Continued and revitalized efforts to mainstream gender equality across agencies are also more important now than ever before. Finally, UN Women's effective, credible delivery depends on the highest accountability standards, oversight, robust risk management, and a zero-tolerance approach to sexual exploitation, abuse, and sexual harassment. We encourage greater openness with the Board about the challenges that you face on this. The UK remains an advocate for the work that UN Women does, and we will continue to defend the principles of gender equality. Thank you.

I thank the distinguished representative from the United Kingdom for her comments. I now have the following three speakers on my list: Colombia, the UAE, and Germany. The distinguished representative from Colombia, you have the floor.

Gracias, señora.

Thank you, Madam President, Madam Executive Director, Excellencies, distinguished delegates. Colombia thanks you for the annual report on the implementation of the strategic plan for UN Women in a global. Context that is ever more challenging for women and girls. We underscored the aggregated results on participation, economic empowerment, elimination of violence and discrimination against women, and we reaffirmed the importance and validity of the mandate of this institution. What's more, we underscore the fact that we thank UN Women for the close collaboration with Colombia that has enabled, among other things, the following results in terms of taxation policies with a gender approach. We have worked with many different regions to increase by 41% the budget allocated for gender equality. Under Women, Peace and Security, UN Women has provided technical support to the first National Plan of Action in this regard adopted in 2024. When it comes to the peace agreement, the UN Women has supported the efforts of the national government on land issues to implement the agreement, including transferring land ownership deeds to rural women. This is in line with the priorities of the government of President Gustavo Petro, focused on gender equality, strengthening provisions for women with a feminist policy to support women and girls in all their diversity and placing them at the heart of the actions of the state. Madam President, the report also lays bare some of the challenges that we must address: the persistence of violence against women, including their digital expressions, underrepresentation of women in decision-making spaces, and lack of social protection with a gender approach. In this regard, it's crucial for the 2026 to 2029 strategic plan to be built on lessons learned to enable us to more efficiently respond to the new challenges and opportunities in a crucial period for the achievement of the Sustainable Development Goals. To achieve this in a context of reforms in this organization, we call for prioritizing programs and actions that support gender equality, avoiding unfunding that would lead to setbacks in these measures, and to engage in efforts to ensure that UN Women is efficient so that it can respond to its triple mandate. Lastly, in this same vein, we reiterate measures taken by UN Women to accelerate gender equality with measures to help to achieve this with all the Sustainable Development Goals. Madam President, Madam Executive Director, the UN Women has been and will remain key in achieving concrete results with our commitments to meaningful equality. You can count on our voice and our work in Colombia to ensure that together we can transform the lives of all women and girls and with this, the future of our societies. Thank you very much, Madam President.
I thank the distinguished representative from Colombia for his comments, and I now give the floor to the distinguished representative from the UAE.

Madam President, Madam Executive Director, colleagues, thank you for your statements and for your unwavering commitment to uplifting women and girls around the world. We commend the Bureau and the Secretariat for their continuous support of this mission and the remarkable results laid out in the Executive Director's penultimate report on the implementation of UN Women's Strategic Plan for 2022 to 2025. The occasion of the 30th anniversary of the Beijing Declaration and Platform for Action offers us a moment to reflect on the global progress made in advancing gender equality and empowering women and girls. As the UN system adjusts to become more fit for purpose and capable of delivering on its mandate in today's world, we must ensure that the hard-won gains over the past 3 decades are at the heart of this reform. This requires a robust institutional framework that places gender equality and the rights of women and girls at its core. This Board, in close coordination with UN Women, plays a critical role in achieving those objectives, and we support UN Women's efforts in this regard, as well as its unique triple mandate. The United Arab Emirates commends UN Women for its achievements over the past year as presented by Executive Director Bahrouz, especially the serious work improving the agency's organizational effectiveness. UN Women's impact, as evidenced by its broad support to 83 countries where it has strengthened gender-responsive norms and garnered the commitment of both public and private institutions addressing the needs of women and girls reaffirms its vital relevance. Achieving these tangible results despite the difficult operating environment is a testament to the Agency's strength and perseverance. The extensive consultations that UN Women has undertaken in preparing the draft Strategic Plan 2026-2029 are critical to further strengthen the Agency's foundation especially in the final years leading up to 2030. In the face of increasing and cascading challenges, it is all the more essential that the Plan garners the support of Member States to ensure its effectiveness. In closing, the UAE will remain a dedicated partner of UN Women, and we look forward to a constructive session with fellow Board Members over the next 2 days. Thank you, Madam President.
I thank the distinguished representative from the UAE, and I now give the floor to the distinguished representative from Germany.

Thank you.

Madam President, Madam Executive Director, Excellencies, dear colleagues, 10 years ago we all together adopted the Agenda 2030, which remains our most important universal guideline for achieving peace, security, prosperity, and justice for all. Germany is firmly committed to the Agenda 2030 and believes that achieving the Sustainable Development Goals requires a greater focus on women and marginalized groups. Women make up half of humanity. Women and girls need equal rights, resources, and representation in society. The fact that they lack rights, resources and representation is not only unfair, but endangers peace, stability and economic potential. Inclusion of all groups of society is not only the right thing to do, it is the smart thing to do. Therefore, our development cooperation remains committed to feminist principles, such as transforming discriminatory structures using an intersectional lens, and the participation of civil society. We commend UN Women for its unwavering commitment to achieving gender equality and empowering women and girls in all their diversity everywhere. The findings in the annual report highlight the significant impact of UN Women's efforts and emphasizes the importance of continuing this work. Despite a decline in core contributions, the organization achieved achieved positive results in 2024. The growing number of supported countries and high program expenditure demonstrate that UN Women has continued to refine its organizational processes and is making significant progress towards achieving the goals of the current strategic plan. However, funding pressures and the need for most— for cost containment mean that work on diversifying diversifying the funding base must continue alongside further program and geographical prioritization measures. The draft strategic plan for 2026 to '29 showcases UN Women's strategic focus. We encourage you to continue on this path. We also commend UN Women's active role in the UNAED process and its readiness for reform. Germany supports the ambition of the UNAED initiative to make the United Nations more efficient, transparent, and effective, and to encourage focus and comparative advantages. UN Women's normative mandate is key for establishing and promoting global standards and norms for gender equality. Also, UN Women's coordination mandate is a strategic advantage. In line with the Gender Equality Acceleration Plan, the organization should therefore continue to leverage its position to push for system-wide gender mainstreaming, fully integrating gender perspectives across all UN agencies and mechanisms. We are convinced that this will also contribute to the effectiveness of those agencies and their programmes. Finally, I would like to thank the management and staff of UN Women for their dedication and hard work in very difficult times. Germany is fully committed to supporting the organization's mission and vision and looks forward to continuing to work together to achieve SDG 5. I thank you very much.

I thank the distinguished representative from Germany for her comments. I have the following 3 speakers on my list now. It's Panama, New Zealand, and Burkina Faso. The distinguished representative from Panama, you have the floor.

Muchas gracias, señora presidenta.

Thank you very much.
I thank the distinguished representative from Panama for his comments, and I now give the floor to the distinguished representative from New Zealand.

Thank you, President, and New Zealand thanks you, Executive Director, and all UN Women staff for your leadership and commitment in what has been another challenging Year for Global Gender Equality. I thank the distinguished representative from New Zealand for her comments, and the remaining speakers on my list are as following: Burkina Faso, Qatar, Bolivia, the Russian Federation, and the European Union. The distinguished representative from Burkina Faso, you have the floor.

Thank you, Madam President. My delegation in particular welcomes the results achieved in the framework of the 2022-2025 Strategic Plan for the implementation of the new 2026-2029 strategy, which addresses current challenges and includes resilience, economic and climate justice. We encourage and support the Executive Director and all of her team. Madam President, despite the achievements of UN Women, there are still many challenges. In a global context marked by crises and conflicts, the effects of climate change, and economic inequalities, women and girls unfortunately and all too often continue to be the worst affected. For its part, Burkina Faso reiterates its commitment to continuing actions to advance women and girls in its public policies, with a particular focus on education, healthcare, and access to economic resources. My delegation reaffirms its support for the principles of the Beijing Declaration and calls for increased resource mobilization to fill the financing shortfall estimated at $420 billion. To fill that gap— filling that gap, rather, would allow UN Women to strengthen its support for countries in difficulties, including those in the Sahel, where the security situation is making inequalities worse. Also, increased international cooperation would help make sure that each woman and girl has the opportunity to fully and with dignity participate in building a prosperous and just future. To conclude, we once again commend UN Women's leadership. They continue to play a key role in technical assistance, advocacy, and resource mobilization for gender equality and the empowerment of women. We encourage UN Women to continue and to strengthen its presence on the ground, including, as we hope— very much hope, in Burkina Faso. Thank you.
Thank the distinguished representative from Burkina Faso for her comments, and I now give the floor to the distinguished representative from Qatar.

Madam President, Excellencies, members of the Executive Board, ladies and gentlemen, we express our gratitude to the President of the Executive Board for her tireless efforts to lead the Board. We commend the driving role of Ms. Sima Bahus, the Executive Director and USG for UN Women, and we commend the tireless efforts made by UN Women for gender equality and the empowerment of women. The thorough report presented to us today regarding the 2022-2025 Strategic Plan demonstrates the many achievements of UN Women and the fundamental role that this entity plays in giving pride of place to gender equality and also to the protection of the rights of women and girls. We also commend the support provided to states to prepare for the review of the Beijing Declaration and Program of Action 30 years after its adoption. The State of Qatar attaches particular importance to the empowerment of women. It occupies pride of place among my country's priorities. Enormous progress has been made indeed in promoting the rights of women in the context of Qatar's National Vision 2030. This is reflected in various political and program initiatives in Qatar that have contributed to the empowerment of women and to strengthening their participation in every area. In conclusion, The State of Qatar will have the honor to host the 2nd World Summit for Social Development in November. This summit will be an opportunity to accelerate global efforts for the empowerment of women. Given the frontline role played by my country in this area and also given the leading role played by women for social development and sustainable development, Through our participation on this executive board, we will continue to cooperate with colleagues to achieve our goals.
Thank you for her comments, and I now give the floor to the distinguished representative from Bolivia.

Muchas gracias, estimada presidenta.

Thank you very much, distinguished president, excellencies, distinguished colleagues. At the outset, we express our gratitude for the report protected by presented by the Executive Director and for the constant commitment of this entity to advancing gender equality and the empowerment of all women and girls the world over. Bolivia, as a plurinational state, recognizes the fundamental value of gender equality, not only as a human right but also as an essential pillar for building just societies with solidarity and sustainability. Our political constitution is one of the most advanced when it comes to rights and clearly establishes equality between men and women and also recognizes the collective rights of our indigenous women, reevaluating their fundamental role in land, culture, and the identity of all indigenous peoples. This commitment has led to public policies that seek to ensure the full and effective participation of women in all parts of life and also through regulations that sanction gender-based violence and promote justice with an intercultural approach. Bolivia has taken up the challenge of building an inclusive development model in which the voices and wisdom of women in all of their diversity are recognized as fundamental to achieve a future with equality, dignity, and well-being for all people. Madam President, the struggle for gender equality is something that cannot be decoupled from the fight for self-determination and social justice for peoples. We cannot remain silent when faced with the situations that we're seeing in other parts of the world. Bolivia expresses its profound sorrow regarding the situation faced by women and girls in Palestine who are victim to disproportionate violence. Faced forced displacement and systemic violations of their human rights. Palestinian women are not only resisting the direct impact of the conflict, but they are also upholding life, protecting their families and communities, and seeking justice in the midst of destruction. My country rejects all forms of violence against women in the context of occupation and armed conflict, and we demand that international humanitarian law be respected and that hostilities be immediately halted, and an emergent— an urgent response from the multilateral system with a gender and humanity-based focus. Madam President, to conclude, we launch an appeal to this Executive Board to shed light on and make a priority Indigenous women and girls, respecting their cultural diversity, their ancestral knowledge, and their indigenous languages, guaranteeing their effective inclusion in all public policies. To broaden support for women and girls in contexts of crisis and conflict, like in Palestine, where human suffering, injustice, and gender-based violence continue to be entrenched. Dear colleagues, gender equality will not be a reality while millions of women and girls live under the shadow of exclusion, violence, and occupation. Indigenous women, Palestinian women, and women from across the world do not just need love, they need justice and a true commitment. Thank you very much.

I thank the distinguished representative from Bolivia for her comments. The final 3 speakers on my list are, as things stand now, the Russian Federation, the European Union, and Egypt. The distinguished representative from the Russian Federation, you have the floor.

Madam President, we thank UN Women and its Executive Director, Sima Bahus, for her strong statement and for the leadership that the organization is shouldering when it comes to achieving gender equality and coordinating the activities to improve the status of women within the UN system. We look forward to further cooperation, and we would like to underscore that we value any of UN Women's cooperation with States when that is carried out with their consent, in the amount and at the level that has been authorized by States, including in the context of cooperation with civil society. Madam President, the Russian Federation has always noted the importance of the entity's mandate to coordinate efforts to achieve gender equality and the empowerment of women. We are convinced that UN Women has everything it needs to successfully continue fulfilling its mandate, even in the difficult financial circumstances. We are grateful to the entity for detailed briefings, expert assessments, and support for states during negotiations, and we're not going to ask the entity to do more, certainly as long as UN Women continues to successfully carry out the task entrusted to it. However, what we should not see in the entity's work is the willful expansion of the mandate with activities on human rights, humanitarian affairs, climate, and other unrelated areas. The empowerment of women must be done on a comprehensive basis and include economic and social measures, as well as support for the family, traditional values, mothers, and children. It is also important that the promotion of women be based on their professional qualities rather than the pursuit of artificial quotas. We are asking for the principle of the division of labor in the UN to be observed and to not duplicate the efforts of other organs and offices in the UN system, particularly given the liquidity crisis. We also call— ask it to not promote dubious initiatives and concepts and to pay more attention to advancing consensus wording that would be acceptable for all UN member states. We are convinced that that is the only effective way to overcome the so-called gender pushbacks. Thank you for your attention.
I thank the distinguished representative from the Russian Federation, and now I give the floor to the representative of the European Union.

Thank you, President, Excellencies, colleagues. I have the honor to deliver this statement on behalf of the European Union as a donor. Let me begin by expressing our gratitude to the Executive Director of UN Women, Mrs. Sima Bahus, and her dedicated staff. Under Mrs. Bahus's leadership, UN Women has continued to advance gender equality and empower women worldwide. In the current global context, UN Women plays an indispensable role in advancing gender equality, championing initiatives that have significantly improved the lives of countless women and girls. Amid growing resistance to gender equality principles and in line with our Gender Action Plan 3, the EU remains committed to promoting and intensifying efforts towards gender equality, ensuring full enjoyment of human rights by all women and girls, contributing to their empowerment.
